text:
Tara (customer-success): P1 from AcmeFinance. Mobile users are seeing SSE connections die after ~10s and sometimes only partial token batches show up in the UI. They also report repeated billing for what looks like replayed tokens. Happening from us-west and eu-west. Can we triage?

Samira (support): They pasted logs — client observes a 204 then reconnect. They use a mobile webview + token proxy. They supplied rough repro steps.

AcmeFinance: steps from our side:
1) POST /v1/auth -> 200, get short-lived token
2) GET /v1/stream Accept: text/event-stream Authorization: Bearer <t>
3) stream emits tokens for ~5-12s
4) connection closed by client, they reconnect with Last-Event-ID header
5) sometimes reconnect -> 401, other times stream resumes but UI shows duplicates

Samira (support): We scanned billing metrics and don't see a backend billing spike, but edge logs show tons of reconnects for their x-req-ids. Pinging runtime+infra. @Jorge @Maya @Chris

Jorge (eng-runtime): Edge gives entries like:

```
edge=usw-12 req=GET /v1/stream status=200 downstream_closed_by_client=1 upstream_closed_by_server=0 duration=11.1s x-req-id=rc_9a1b
```

Jorge (eng-runtime): There are reconnects with Last-Event-ID present. Token validation shows occasional 401 on reconnects; looks like their token TTL may be very short (~10s). Need customer confirm token TTL.

Maya (eng-infra): rolled edge-proxy v3.2.1 ~6h ago (deploy-bot shows successful rollout). That might change TCP/window semantics.

deploy-bot: deploy/edge-proxy v3.2.1 -> success; rollout started 2024-11-11T16:00:00Z

Chris (oncall): Many middleboxes drop idle HTTP connections after ~10s (esp mobile carriers/webviews). ALB/NLB defaults are usually much higher but can't rely on client path. Do we emit keepalive bytes?

Samira (support): Customer said their webview library enforces a 10s idle socket kill. They asked if we recommend comment pings or application-level ping events.

Jorge (eng-runtime): Best practice for flaky clients: send non-disruptive bytes frequently. SSE comment pings (a line starting with a colon) are simplest: they keep intermediaries happy without being parsed as events. Recommend every 8s. If you need resume semantics tied to ids, include regular `id:` lines too. Also, server-side resume should avoid re-emitting the last-delivered token if client expects exclusive resume.

Maya (eng-infra): Notes:
- comment ping (":\n\n") is small and usually prevents proxies from treating the stream as idle.
- Some customer-side proxies will still drop aggressively, but bytes help.
- We can also emit a tiny event (event: ping) if you want visible pings.

Jorge (eng-runtime): Example pseudocode to add server-side ping:

```
// every 8s push a comment ping
setInterval(() => {
  res.write(":\\n\\n"); // SSE comment ping
}, 8000);

// periodically write id so Last-Event-ID works
res.write(`id: ${current_offset}\\n`);
```

Samira (support): Why are duplicates appearing after reconnect?

Jorge (eng-runtime): Two causes: 1) client reconnects and we resume inclusively from the supplied Last-Event-ID, which can replay the last token; 2) the client UI applies the resumed token incorrectly and doesn't dedupe. Server convention should be exclusive resume: if Last-Event-ID=42, resume at 43. We'll add a flag to switch to exclusive resume by default.

Chris (oncall): For reproducing outside their webview, ask them to run a raw curl test to avoid client-wrapper bugs:

```
curl -N \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=..." --no-buffer
```

Then after the stream closes, reconnect with `-H "Last-Event-ID: <id>"` and paste results. Also capture tcpdump if possible.

Samira (support): Billing pinged: how do reconnects affect billing?

billing-bot: usage is token-count based at generation completion. If the model re-generates tokens after a resume and they are identical but re-emitted, they may be counted twice. We have some server-side dedupe heuristics if the same request id + event id match, but client replays can still cause charged duplicates.

Maya (eng-infra): Mitigations we can deploy for this account immediately (with opt-in):
- enable server-side comment pings at 8s for their sessions to fight client socket killers
- accept a short reconnect grace for recently-expired tokens when reconnect includes same x-req-id (e.g., <=5s)
- toggle resume behavior to exclusive so we don't resend last event by default

Jorge (eng-runtime): I'll draft a small change to resume semantics (exclusive resume) behind a feature flag and add a dedupe header marker on events. Opening PR shortly.

Jorge (eng-runtime): PR drafted: https://git.redwood.ai/pr/2897 (resume-exclusive + dedupe header)

Maya (eng-infra): Created infra ticket INF-512 for per-account ping opt-in and auth-grace. Will coordinate with security and billing for approvals.

security: we need written customer consent before we change session behavior per-account. Also verify token-grace doesn't open replay window beyond intended TTL.

Samira (support): Actions for customer:
- run curl repro and attach tcpdump + headers + x-req-id
- we can enable comment pings for their sessions if they approve and we'll flip the resume-feature-flag in a controlled rollout
- we'll apply a one-time billing credit for any duplicated charged tokens while we fix this

AcmeFinance: okay, will run curl and attach logs. They confirm token TTL is currently 10s. They opt into temporary comment-ping enable.

Tara (customer-success): Customer opted in. Marking P1 until we've completed change and verified. Thanks all. :pray:

Chris (oncall): Long-term suggestion: platform default of emitting comment pings at ~8s + doc updates about Last-Event-ID semantics and token TTL best practices. Filing follow-up RFC ticket.

Samira (support): I'll update this thread when tcpdump arrives. Keeping thread open until postmortem.
